claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The evidence consists of a bystander turning and pointing to a blue sedan, which constitutes nonverbal conduct. Under FRE 801(a)(2), nonverbal conduct is only a statement if intended as an assertion; absent clear intent, pointing is typically treated as circumstantial evidence rather than hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that a bystander turned and pointed to a blue sedan

arguments.text: The pointing is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, specifically that the blue sedan was responsible for the hit and run. If the conduct is deemed an assertion, this satisfies the third prong of FRE 801(c), supporting a hearsay classification.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) - Offered to prove truth of matter asserted
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of which car was responsible for the hit and run, the fact that a bystander turned and pointed to a blue sedan.

arguments.text: The narrative describes the evidence merely as the fact that a bystander turned and pointed, lacking any indication that the bystander intended to communicate or assert a fact. Without intent to assert, the conduct falls outside the definition of a hearsay statement, attacking the claim.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a)(2) intent requirement for nonverbal conduct
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that a bystander turned and pointed to a blue sedan
